title: Web screen and controls
lead: Choose a theme, change a source or setting, and inspect the result. This page follows the Web screen; the implementation guide explains the corresponding SDK code.

items.label: Implementation guide: configuration, UI changes and FAQ

blocks.text: Screen layout and language

Choose a language and theme at the top. The video and construction code are followed by source and playback controls, UI and casting controls, player state and event logs, and the configuration editors.

The initial source is VOD HLS with the Live (DVR) theme. Autoplay and mute are enabled; control autohide is off. A theme named Live can also play on-demand media. Theme buttons do not select the streaming format.

blocks.caption: The Web app with its theme selector, video, construction code and operation panels. The layout adapts to the available width.

items: Open the Web app. If autoplay does not start, press Play. Playback starts muted; choose a suitable volume before unmuting.
Choose the display language at the top. Keep the same source while comparing themes, then use the source controls to try audio, subtitles or thumbnails.

Read the live player state and event log after each operation. Settings marked reload or recreate remain drafts until the corresponding Apply action completes; instant and UI settings apply when the input change is committed.

blocks.text: Display language

Switch between Japanese and English at the top. SDK identifiers such as autoplay stay in English so that you can look them up in the API reference. The browser remembers the language for the app and guide.

Changing language rebuilds the Player Config form and discards edits that have not been applied. Apply the changes you need first. Changing language alone does not reset the state readout, event log or applied settings.
Compare themes and construction code
Ways to customize the UI

rows: Default UI
Default (Bitmovin) uses the standard desktop component tree through the app's DefaultUIFactory wrapper. Start here when comparing a custom layout.
Default UI + CSS
Neon, Glass, Sunset, Bold and Mono retain the standard structure and change colors, sizes and other styling through CSS.
Custom UI
Live (DVR), Sports, Binge, Cinema, Compact, Premiere, Creator and Studio change the choice and arrangement of components.

blocks.text: Available themes

rows: Default (Bitmovin)
Compare behavior against the standard UI.
Neon
Apply bright colors and gradients to the standard UI.
Glass
Show a translucent control bar.
Sunset
Apply a warm gradient palette.
Bold
Show larger controls with high contrast.
Mono
Use a monochrome palette with the standard UI.
Live (DVR)
Show the live edge, wall-clock time, distance behind live and 10-second skip controls.
Sports
Overlay sample scores and player information. The INFO button shows them again.
Binge
Try skipping the sample intro from 5 to 18 seconds and moving to the next episode near the end.
Cinema
Use a central play control and a slim control bar.
Compact
Use a compact single row without a central playback overlay.
Premiere
Show a title, full-width seek bar, settings menu and recommendations at the end.
Creator
Show a title and full-width seek bar with a row for playback, volume, time and settings.
Studio
Show a title and a single-row seek bar between the time labels.

blocks.text: Compare the video and code

items: Start VOD HLS and select Default (Bitmovin). Check the current time, pause/resume, volume and seek bar before changing the UI.
Select Neon, then return to Default. Compare the seek-bar color, button appearance and control-bar background while checking that playback continues. These themes share the same component tree.
Select Premiere, Creator and Studio on the same source. Compare the title, current/remaining time, settings gear and seek-bar position. These themes build different component trees.
Open the construction code beside the video. Its difference summary explains the changed components; the source path below the code identifies the factory or stylesheet to inspect.

In UI settings, change Speed item in settings gear while using Premiere. Reopen the gear menu and check the applied UIConfig overrides beside the video. Change the setting back and confirm the item returns.

blocks.caption: The Premiere composition. Compare its controls and layout with Default while keeping the same source; the code beside the player describes the selected composition.

blocks.text: Switching a theme keeps the player and source and replaces the UI. Construction code is a read-only excerpt. The UIConfig override view lists only values explicitly changed in the GUI; it excludes theme defaults, sample metadata, autohide and casting options, PlayerConfig and SourceConfig. Neither view saves the complete app state.
Try theme-specific controls

rows: Sports with a playing source
Wait for the sample score and player-information overlays to hide, then press INFO to show them again. Their content is supplied by sportsData.ts; it is not a live sports feed.
Binge with VOD HLS

During the sample intro from 5 to 18 seconds, use Skip Intro and check the playback position. Near the end, inspect Next episode and the Next-up card. Continuous play controls automatic advancement through the configured playlist.
Premiere, Creator or Studio with VOD

Open the gear menu and compare speed, quality and audio choices. Available choices depend on the source and UI settings. Finish playback to inspect the recommendation overlay, then select a recommendation and check the loaded source.
Live (DVR) with VOD, then an available live preset
Compare elapsed/total time on VOD with the LIVE and time labels on a live stream. The theme name does not make a source live or provide a rewind window; those depend on the loaded media.

blocks.text: Return to a comparison baseline

Selecting Default changes the UI composition; it does not reset the source, playback settings or UIConfig overrides. Restore the toggles changed during an experiment, keep Autohide controls off while inspecting the layout, and select the same source before comparing again. Reloading the page restores the app's initial in-memory settings. The selected app language and any enabled Player UI storage preferences or resume positions can survive a reload.
To add or move controls or edit a skin, follow the source paths below the construction code and the implementation guide.
Sources, playback, audio and subtitles

The apps use several test streams. Pages includes short Big Buck Bunny clips for basic VOD controls; local and native examples also use external HLS, DASH and live streams. Available tracks, duration and rewind range depend on the source.

blocks.caption: Source selection. VOD is on-demand media; Live selects live streams.

blocks.text: Choose a test source

rows: VOD HLS
Play the 60-second Big Buck Bunny sample over HLS.
VOD DASH
Play the same 60-second sample over DASH and compare the formats.
Live DASH + DVR
Use an external public live stream to check rewinding, multiple audio tracks and subtitles.
Live HLS
Play an external public HLS live stream.
VOD + Sprites
Check image thumbnails on the seek bar.
VOD + Multi-audio
Choose between two audio tracks.
VOD + Subtitles
Enable and display separately loaded WebVTT subtitles.

blocks.text: The provider controls the availability, content and rewind window of external live streams. This guide does not guarantee their future availability. In local development, unconfigured feature presets are disabled and list the required environment-variable names.
Basic playback and seeking

Use the controls inside the video for play/pause, volume and fullscreen. The seek bar represents the whole video for on-demand media and the available rewind window for live media. On custom themes, a single click on the video surface toggles playback.

With Double-click set to Fullscreen, a double-click on the video surface toggles fullscreen. With Seek ±10s, a double-click on the left half moves back 10 seconds and the right half moves forward 10 seconds. Targets are clamped to the video duration or live DVR window. Default (Bitmovin) uses the stock UI behavior.
Switch audio tracks

items: Select VOD + Multi-audio.
Select a theme with an audio menu, such as Default or Premiere.
Open the player settings menu and choose another Audio track.
Unmute and adjust the volume if you want to listen.

blocks.text: Both bundled audio tracks contain the same nonverbal soundtrack at different volumes. The en/de labels are test metadata for track selection, not English and German translations.
Display subtitles

items: Select VOD + Subtitles.
Choose English in the subtitle menu inside the player.
Move to a time containing a cue and check its display. Select the disabled option to check that it disappears.

blocks.text: The subtitle text comes from Sintel and has been retimed for a short test. It does not describe Big Buck Bunny. Available subtitle and audio lists can change when you select another source.
Check seek thumbnails

items: Select VOD + Sprites.
Move the pointer along the seek bar inside the video.
Check that the displayed time and image change with the position.

blocks.text: A sprite sheet combines several small images into one file. A WebVTT file maps times to image regions, and the player displays the corresponding region. Seek scrub-preview in UI settings is a separate feature: it controls whether the playing video follows the scrubber while dragging.
Set the initial playback position

rows: Start an on-demand clip after its beginning
options.startOffset = 5 seconds; timeline reference = start
After source reload, playback starts near 5 seconds and then advances. This is a loading setting, rather than a seek command applied to current playback.
Start near the end of an on-demand clip
options.startOffset = -10 seconds; timeline reference = end
For the 60-second Pages clip, the requested initial position is near 50 seconds.
Start behind the live edge
options.startOffset = -20 seconds; timeline reference = end
Start behind the available live edge. The source must offer a sufficient rewind window; an out-of-range position is limited to the available range.

items: Choose the source first. To make start-position comparisons easier to interpret, turn off Resume VOD position and avoid a URL timestamp for this experiment.

Open Source in Player Config, enter the offset and select its reference, then press Reload the source to apply. Confirm SourceLoaded in the event log and compare the initial time on the video or the Player state readout. With autoplay, playback continues while you read it.
Refresh Show applied configuration code and inspect sourceConfig.options. Other applied source fields stay in place during this reload.
Clear options.startOffset, set the reference to its default option, and reload to remove these overrides. Selecting a source preset again also clears its source overrides.

blocks.text: The Playback panel's Reload at offset button always uses an end reference. Use the Source editor when you need to choose start or end explicitly. A live start position is constrained by the actual manifest and the source's current availability, rather than the duration of the bundled on-demand clip.
Choose initial audio and subtitle languages

Set initial language preferences in Playback and recreate the player. These fields take a single string, not a comma-separated list or JSON array. To switch tracks during playback, use the player menu instead.

items: Choose VOD + Multi-audio and a theme with an audio menu, such as Premiere. In Playback, enter de for audioLanguage and press Recreate the player to apply. Check the selected audio track in the player menu, then unmute to compare its sound. The bundled language labels are test metadata, as explained above.

Switch to Default, which includes subtitle controls, then choose VOD + Subtitles. In Playback, enter en for subtitleLanguage and recreate. At a time containing a cue, check the rendered text and the selected subtitle in the menu. In local development this preset needs its subtitle URL configured before use.
Refresh the applied code and inspect playerConfig.playback.audioLanguage or subtitleLanguage. A matching track must exist in the selected source; a preference does not add a missing language.

Clear the language field and recreate to remove the preference override. To turn off the current subtitle immediately, choose the disabled option in the player's subtitle menu; removing a startup preference is a different action.

blocks.text: Selecting a source again

Source changes such as a title or start position retain the other applied source settings when the same source reloads. Selecting a preset through a source button or an end-of-playback recommendation clears the previous source overrides, even if you select the same preset again.

The basic source picker selects the listed presets. To use a different HLS or DASH URL, open SDK settings, APIs and events and edit SourceConfig.hls or SourceConfig.dash, or pass a source object through Commands → PlayerAPI.load. The Web implementation guide explains these paths and how to configure a reusable source in code.

items.label: Web implementation guide: use your own stream

blocks.text: Player and source settings
The Player Config form groups settings by when they take effect. Use the SDK editor below it for additional properties, objects, callbacks and API calls.

blocks.caption: SourceConfig fields. The Apply button is below the complete configuration panel.

blocks.text: How changes take effect

rows: Immediate
Calls a runtime API when you commit the input. Includes Player API, dynamic adaptation and low-latency controls.
Reload
Reloads the source with its title, description, poster and start-position settings.
Recreate
Creates a new player with the edited PlayerConfig.

blocks.text: The separate control panel also contains live rewind, UI and casting controls. Open or close a configuration group using its heading. Playback and source groups start open; creation groups start closed.
Try an immediate setting

items: Open Player API and inspect current values such as volume and mute.
Change one field, then commit it by leaving the input or using its selector. Inputs apply on a change event, not on every keystroke.
Check the actual change in volume, playback speed or view mode. Changing volume may unmute the player and make audio audible.
Compare another value while retaining the same playback.

blocks.text: Fullscreen and PiP require a supported environment and a user gesture. Some runtime fields do not implement removal of a value when cleared. Leaving aspect ratio, poster, resolution limits or latency values empty does not necessarily restore the SDK default.
Apply source settings

items: Change title in Source. Use a theme such as Premiere that displays the title.
Change description, poster, startOffset and its reference if needed.
Press Reload the source to apply.
Check the on-video display and start position after reloading.

blocks.text: Reload and recreation edits remain staged until their respective Apply button is pressed. The button is disabled when there are no changes. A source reload retains the other applied source settings.
Set stream URLs, subtitles and thumbnails

In the SDK editor, choose SourceConfig.hls for an HLS preset or SourceConfig.dash for a DASH preset, edit the URL and apply it. To supply a complete source object, use PlayerAPI.load. If both URLs are present, the SDK selects the playback technology.

items.label: Source URL, external subtitle, thumbnail, poster and DRM settings

blocks.text: Complete required fields together before applying an object or array in the SDK editor. Selecting a source preset again clears SourceConfig overrides. PlayerConfig settings survive source selection, so inspect both applied configurations when comparing conditions.
Apply initial settings

items: Open the groups you need, such as Playback, Adaptation or Buffer.
Change a small number of values to compare.
Press Recreate the player to apply.
Check applied values and playback behavior after loading again.

blocks.text: Configuration groups

items.label: Configuration groups and their SDK targets

blocks.text: Initial display values in the settings catalog are form fallbacks when an applied value cannot be read. They are not SDK defaults, current effective values or recommendations. A Tweaks checkbox documented as false does not establish that the SDK default is false.

items.label: Timeout units, validation and retry settings

blocks.text: Compare automatic video quality
To compare automatic quality selection, select VOD DASH and Premiere, then choose Auto in the quality menu. The bundled Pages stream has 180p and 360p renditions.

items: Set dynamic Adaptation → resolution.maxSelectableVideoHeight to 180 and leave the field to apply it.
Refresh the applied code and check maxSelectableVideoHeight. Allow buffered video to play out, then inspect the video resolution and requests in the browser media tools.
Restore 360 to allow the highest bundled rendition. An empty field does not remove this runtime limit; reload the page to start without the applied edits.

items.label: Bitrate, resolution and startup-quality examples and limitations

blocks.text: Compare retained media buffers

Buffer targets are durations in seconds. Player API changes the video forward target immediately; Buffer initial settings apply separate audio/video and forward/backward targets when the player is recreated.

items: Set Player API → buffer target forward (s) to 10 and refresh the applied code.
Use Read state → PlayerAPI.buffer.getLevel with the media and buffer type to read the current level. The input is a target, not a live buffer gauge.
Restore the previous numeric target. Leaving this runtime field empty does not undo the API call.

items.label: Audio/video buffers, startup thresholds and memory tradeoffs

blocks.text: Set request timeouts and retries
Edit timeouts in Network and retries in Tweaks, then recreate the player. These settings control individual requests; they do not set the total time before a playback error.

items.label: Request types, units and retry behavior

items: Select VOD DASH, open the browser Network tools and record the original settings.

Apply the changes. Add controlled latency to test a timeout, or temporarily block the manifest to compare retries. Inspect actual request counts and intervals in Network; the app event log is not an HTTP trace.
Remove browser throttling or blocking. Clear numeric overrides and recreate the player; restore checkboxes to their original state. Reload the source and check normal playback.

blocks.text: SDK settings, API calls and events
Open the SDK editor below Player Config. Search by the public API name and choose configuration, command, state or event. Each entry links to the official reference.

items: Choose a configuration entry such as SourceConfig.title, select a type if requested, enter a value and apply it. The editor shows whether this reloads the source, recreates the player or rebuilds the UI.
Add array items or dictionary properties as needed. Complete required fields on the parent object before applying an entry. An edited array replaces the whole array.
Use “Remove this override” to return to the app base value. Unrelated overrides are retained.
For a method, enter arguments and run the API or read state. The result appears below its generated code.
For events, operate the player and check the count and recent content. Recreating the player clears the old subscriptions and history.

blocks.text: Selecting undefined for an optional configuration property omits it from the SDK input. A successful submission only means the editor sent the setting; use state, events and playback to check the result.

items.label: Object editing, override precedence and omitted properties

blocks.caption: The SDK editor searches public paths and provides inputs for the selected setting. This example edits the source title.

blocks.text: Edit a callback

A callback is a function that the SDK invokes. Select the function input type, use the displayed parameter names and return type, and enter its JavaScript body. Enable Allow this callback to run in this page after Apply, then apply the setting. For network.preprocessHttpRequest, this body returns the request unchanged:
return Promise.resolve(request);

The function runs as JavaScript in this page. The log reports calls and return-type mismatches. To recover from a callback that leaves a request unfinished, remove its override and recreate the player.

items.label: Callback context, native-HLS limitations and playback-technology selection

blocks.caption: The request callback has editable code, a published signature and an explicit execution control. The SDK invokes it after Apply.

blocks.text: Use SDK objects and inspect runtime state
Where an SDK object is required, choose a public constructor or a current SDK instance. Certificate buffers accept hexadecimal or Base64 bytes. Use JSON only where the SDK accepts data objects.

Read PlayerAPI.getConfig or PlayerAPI.getSource to inspect the supplied settings. A returned instance or function can be selected in later calls; retrieve it again after its owning player is replaced. Event counts remain when older log entries expire. “Clear event history” or recreating the player clears the record.

items.label: SDK-object lifetimes, UI ownership and source metadata precedence

blocks.text: The existence of a field does not establish that it applies in the current environment or has been verified on every platform. Use compatible media and environments for conditional settings such as TV, DRM, advertising and native HLS.
Compare a command with a state read and an event

items: Choose Commands, search for PlayerAPI.pause and run the API. The video should pause; use the player controls or PlayerAPI.play to resume.
Choose Read state and PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime, then Read state. Read it again after playback advances. The result is a snapshot, rather than a continuously updated control.
Choose Events and select a relevant event. Operate the player and inspect the event log below. Counts and payloads change when that event occurs; choosing its name does not create an event.

blocks.text: Read and copy applied configuration
This view shows applied Player and source settings, runtime values handled by the GUI and UI overrides. It excludes draft edits. License values are removed or replaced with placeholders.

items: Wait for the source to load and apply the settings to inspect.
Open the applied-code view below the form and refresh it after any later changes. Copy retrieves the latest settings; if clipboard access fails, select and copy the text manually.
Compare it with the theme construction code beside the video: one shows applied settings, the other shows the UI component layout. Neither exports the entire app.

blocks.caption: Applied configuration code after the source has loaded and Refresh code has run. The Player key is a placeholder; draft edits are excluded.

items.label: Implementation guide: reproduce the configuration and UI changes in your app

blocks.text: UI behavior and saved preferences
Keep the same source while changing UI behavior. Restore the original value after each comparison so that stored preferences, URL start positions and source offsets do not overlap unexpectedly.

blocks.caption: The UI settings panel. Each checkbox or input changes a particular behavior of the current theme; some settings require a compatible source or browser feature.

blocks.text: Available UI settings

rows: Autohide controls
Hide the bar after inactivity. Initially off; applies to every theme, including Default.
Seek scrub-preview
Make the video follow the scrubber while dragging. When off, seek after release.
Keep bar on hover
With autohide enabled, keep the bar visible while the pointer is over the player.
Speed item in settings gear
Toggle the playback-speed selector. Check it in a theme with a settings menu.
Snap seeks to markers
Snap a seek near a marker to its position.
Fullscreen on first play
Enter fullscreen when the first playback begins through the play button. This is difficult to observe with the default autoplay behavior.
Keep subtitles in view
Keep overflowing subtitles inside the display area. Use a source with subtitles.
Disable UI storage
Disable Player UI localStorage access, including preferences and resume positions.
Snap range (%)
Set the snapping distance as a percentage of seek-bar width.
CEA-608 small-player px
Set the player-height threshold for small-player placement of compatible captions.
Remember playback preferences
Store volume, mute and playback speed in the browser. Initially off. Requires UI storage; a choice already made with the preferences switch takes precedence.
Resume VOD position
Store VOD positions and resume on a later source load. Initially off. Requires UI storage; live streams are excluded.
Read timestamp from URL
Read a VOD start position such as t=30 from the query or fragment. Initially on. Reload the source after changing this setting because it applies on the first source load after UI creation.
Preference switch in default settings
Show the playback-preferences switch in Default and CSS themes. Initially off. Hidden when UI storage is disabled. Custom component layouts do not add this switch.
Player UI language
Use auto for the browser language, or en, de, es, fr, nl or pt. Other languages fall back to English. Separate from the app Japanese/English selector.
Follow subtitle language
Use the selected subtitle language for Player UI. Initially off. If its translation is unavailable, use the configured UI language.

blocks.text: The sample chapter markers are at 120, 360 and 600 seconds. The 60-second Pages sample cannot reach them, so it cannot demonstrate marker snapping. The CEA-608 setting also cannot be checked using only the separate WebVTT subtitle file.

Changing a checkbox or number rebuilds the active theme UI. Settings that do not recreate the player retain the current playback session. Changing a value on media that cannot exercise the feature is not evidence that the feature worked.

The construction panel also shows applied UIConfig overrides as code. Its Player UI language is separate from the app language. Changes rebuild the UI without recreating the Player; source-load settings such as timestamp links require a subsequent source load.
Compare controls during playback

items: Select VOD HLS and Premiere. Note the current time and the UI setting values you want to restore. A UI setting change rebuilds the controls while keeping the Player instance; it does not require the Source or Player Config Apply buttons.

Turn on Autohide controls. Move the pointer outside the video and wait for the controls to hide. Then turn on Keep bar on hover and compare while the pointer remains over the video. Return the switches to their recorded values.

Turn off Speed item in settings gear, then open the gear menu. The playback-speed selector disappears. Turn it on again to restore the selector. This removes a UI control; it does not disable the Player API playbackSpeed field.
Turn Seek scrub-preview off and drag the seek bar: the seek applies after release. Turn it on and compare the video while dragging. Thumbnail images are a separate feature of VOD + Sprites.

Enter de in Player UI language and leave the field. Check the player control labels, then return to en or auto. The app's English/Japanese selector remains separate. Turn Follow subtitle language off when comparing a fixed UI language.

blocks.text: The construction-code panel displays the applied UIConfig overrides, such as playbackSpeedSelectionEnabled and localization.language. The applied configuration export below Player Config includes the same UI overrides. Changing themes retains these overrides. Numeric UI fields need an explicit previous value to restore them; empty input is treated as zero, rather than removing an override.
Check startup and saved-position behavior

rows: Enter fullscreen at first play
Turn autoplay off in Playback and recreate. Enable Fullscreen on first play in UI settings, then press the player play button.
The browser must allow fullscreen from that user action. Restore the UI switch and the earlier autoplay value; changing autoplay requires recreation.
Start a VOD from a URL timestamp
Open the Web app URL with ?t=30 and use VOD HLS. To compare with the option off, disable Read timestamp from URL and select the VOD HLS source again.

Check the initial time, not a later time after autoplay has advanced. Remove t from the URL and restore the switch afterwards. Saved resume positions and Source start offsets should be excluded from this comparison.
Inspect preference storage
Use Default or a CSS theme. Keep Disable UI storage off, enable Remember playback preferences and optionally Preference switch in default settings, then change volume, mute or speed.
Check the switch in the gear menu and the stored state in the browser's storage tools. A prior choice made in that switch can override the initial preference setting.
Compare VOD resume
Keep UI storage enabled, enable Resume VOD position, play into a VOD and load the same source again.
Compare the starting position with the option off, using a URL without t and no Source start offset. This applies to on-demand media, not live streams.

blocks.text: Disable UI storage prevents the UI from using browser localStorage; it is separate from Player Config storage.disableStorageApi and does not mean that already saved browser data has been deleted. Restore the switches you changed. For an experiment independent of saved UI state, enable Disable UI storage. The GUI has no button that clears stored preferences.
Continuous play

The Binge playlist advances through configured presets in this order: VOD HLS, VOD DASH, VOD + Multi-audio and VOD + Subtitles. Automatic advancement is initially enabled. When disabled, use the Next button near the end. Skip Intro appears from 5 to 18 seconds. Those are sample times, not automatically detected intro boundaries.
Picture-in-Picture and external displays

Picture-in-Picture, AirPlay and Cast depend on the browser, operating system and receiver. First check that the local playback is working; enabling a button does not establish a connection to another device.

rows: Playback panel PiP toggle
Change the player view mode. Browser and OS support are required.
Casting & PiP: PiP button
Add a small-window button to custom UIs. It is hidden in unsupported environments.
AirPlay button
Add AirPlay to custom UIs. A compatible Safari environment is required.
Chromecast button
Add Cast to custom UIs. The player is recreated to enable remotecontrol. A compatible receiver is required.

blocks.text: Default and the CSS themes use the standard UI structure, which already includes these buttons. The add/remove checkboxes change the custom UI component trees. Enabling a checkbox does not make a button or receiver available unless the browser, connection and device requirements are met.

The Cast control is wired to remotecontrol using the default receiver. The existence of its settings is separate from verification on a physical receiver. TV remote navigation and VR playback controls are not provided as features of the current Web screen.
